Estimate Standardized Regression Coefficients and the Corresponding Likelihood-Based Confidence Intervals

Source: R/betaLB-beta-lb.R
BetaLB.Rd

Estimates the standardized regression coefficients and their profile likelihood confidence intervals for independently sampled random regressors.

Usage

BetaLB(
  object,
  type = "mvn",
  alpha = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
  std_y = TRUE,
  std_x = NULL,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

object

Object of class lm. Unweighted, full-rank, scalar-response fit with an intercept, a stored model frame, no offsets, and a positive residual variance.

type

Character string. Calibration of the likelihood-ratio cutoff. "mvn" (default) assumes multivariate normality. "robust" uses the empirical fourth moments.

alpha

Numeric vector. Significance level \(\alpha\).

std_y

Logical. Standardize \(y\). With std_y = FALSE, \(y\) is left in its original units (\(b_j \sigma_{x_j}\)).

std_x

Character vector or NULL. Names of the regressors to standardize. NULL (default) standardizes all regressors; character(0) standardizes none (\(b_j / \sigma_y\)). Leaving a dummy variable out keeps its 0-1 contrast.

control

Named list. maxeval is the evaluation budget per endpoint (default 10000L); tolerance is the normalized verification tolerance (default 1e-8).

Value

Returns an object of class betalb which is a list with the following elements:

call

Function call.

args

Function arguments.

lm_process

Sample size, number of regressors, and regressor names of the lm object.

data

Sample covariance matrix, units, and the estimated asymptotic covariance matrices of its elements.

est

Vector of standardized slopes.

intervals

Data frame with one row per slope and significance level: the estimate, the lower and upper limits, the status of each endpoint, and the calibration used.

diagnostics

Solver diagnostics of each endpoint.

Details

Partition the covariance matrix of the outcome and the regressors as $$\boldsymbol{\Sigma} = \begin{pmatrix} \sigma^{2}_{y} & \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{yx}^{\prime} \\ \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{yx} & \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x} \end{pmatrix}.$$ The standardized regression slopes are $$\beta^{\ast}_{j} = \beta_{j} \frac{\sigma_{x_{j}}}{\sigma_{y}}, \quad \boldsymbol{\beta} = \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x}^{-1} \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{yx}.$$ Let \(\tilde{\boldsymbol{S}}\) be the sample covariance matrix with divisor \(n\), \(q\) the number of variables, and $$F \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right) = n \left[ \log \left| \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right| - \log \left| \tilde{\boldsymbol{S}} \right| + \operatorname{tr} \left( \tilde{\boldsymbol{S}} \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1} \right) - q \right]$$ the Gaussian likelihood-ratio statistic of \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\) against \(\tilde{\boldsymbol{S}}\). For a target \(\theta = g \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right)\), here \(\beta^{\ast}_{j}\), the \(100 \left( 1 - \alpha \right) \%\) interval is $$\left\{ \theta_{0} : \min_{\boldsymbol{\Sigma} : g \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right) = \theta_{0}} F \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right) \leq c \, \chi^{2}_{1, 1 - \alpha} \right\}.$$ With type = "mvn", \(c = 1\). With type = "robust", $$c = \frac{\boldsymbol{b}^{\prime} \hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{ADF}} \boldsymbol{b}}{\boldsymbol{b}^{\prime} \hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{N}} \boldsymbol{b}}, \quad \boldsymbol{b} = \frac{\partial g}{\partial \operatorname{vech} \left( \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \right)},$$ evaluated at \(\tilde{\boldsymbol{S}}\), where \(\hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{N}}\) and \(\hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{ADF}}\) are the normal-theory and the fourth-moment estimates of the asymptotic covariance matrix of \(\sqrt{n} \operatorname{vech} \left( \tilde{\boldsymbol{S}} \right)\). For a vector target of dimension \(r\), \(c\) is the largest generalized eigenvalue of \(\boldsymbol{B} \hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{ADF}} \boldsymbol{B}^{\prime}\) relative to \(\boldsymbol{B} \hat{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}}_{\mathrm{N}} \boldsymbol{B}^{\prime}\) and the cutoff has \(r\) degrees of freedom. The effect size functions use the same statistic with their own \(g\).

The intervals are the sets of parameter values that a likelihood-ratio test of the covariance matrix of the response and the regressors does not reject at the significance level alpha. With type = "mvn", the divisor-\(n\) Gaussian covariance likelihood and its chi-square cutoff are used. With type = "robust", the cutoff is scaled by the sample fourth moments of the data, so that the intervals are robust to non-normality. These are asymptotic procedures, without a finite-sample coverage guarantee. The solver runs once per significance level. The effect size functions (RSqLB(), SCorLB(), PCorLB(), DeltaRSqLB(), FSqLB(), and DiffBetaLB()) take the object returned by this function and use its type and control.

References

Dudgeon, P. (2017). Some improvements in confidence intervals for standardized regression coefficients. Psychometrika, 82(4), 928–951. doi:10.1007/s11336-017-9563-z

See also

Other Beta Likelihood-Based Functions: DeltaRSqLB(), DiffBetaLB(), FSqLB(), PCorLB(), RSqLB(), SCorLB(), SCorSqLB()

Examples

# Data ---------------------------------------------------------------------
data("nas1982", package = "betaLB")

# Fit Model in lm ----------------------------------------------------------
object <- stats::lm(
  formula = QUALITY ~ NARTIC + PCTGRT + PCTSUPP,
  data = nas1982
)

# BetaLB -------------------------------------------------------------------
std <- BetaLB(object = object, alpha = 0.05)

## Methods -----------------------------------------------------------------
print(x = std)
#> Call:
#> BetaLB(object = object, alpha = 0.05)
#> 
#> Standardized regression slopes with MVN likelihood intervals:
#>            est   2.5%  97.5%
#> NARTIC  0.4951 0.3423 0.6394
#> PCTGRT  0.3915 0.2395 0.5426
#> PCTSUPP 0.2632 0.1179 0.4148
summary(object = std)
#> Call:
#> BetaLB(object = object, alpha = 0.05)
#> 
#> Standardized regression slopes with MVN likelihood intervals:
#>            est   2.5%  97.5%
#> NARTIC  0.4951 0.3423 0.6394
#> PCTGRT  0.3915 0.2395 0.5426
#> PCTSUPP 0.2632 0.1179 0.4148
coef(object = std)
#>    NARTIC    PCTGRT   PCTSUPP 
#> 0.4951451 0.3914887 0.2632477 
confint(object = std, level = 0.95)
#>             2.5 %    97.5 %
#> NARTIC  0.3423306 0.6394250
#> PCTGRT  0.2395150 0.5426127
#> PCTSUPP 0.1178587 0.4148453
